summary: Hokai (1768–1834) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Hogetsu and Zuihe.
Hokei Izumi (1884–1947) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Bunyiu Nanjio and served as a professor at Otani University from circa 1923 to 1947.
Hoko Kuwana is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (attested 2015). Kuwana held a post at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Holly Gayley works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Harvard University as a doctoral candidate from circa 2002 to 2009 and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder circa 2008.

Holmes Welch (1924–1981) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed a B.A. and M.A. at Harvard University (circa 1940–1957) and taught as a Dozent at Harvard (circa 1964–1974) and Yale University.

Hong Luo specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Luo earned a PhD from Peking University in 2007, worked at the China Tibetology Research Center (2007–2017), became a religious studies professor at Sichuan University in 2018, and Hamburg (attested 2026).

Hongyue Guo specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Guo completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and also studied under teacher Xubang Qi.

Honsho Ueda (b. 1937) is a Buddhist studies scholar. Ueda held posts at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1963 and 1992), Minobusan University (attested 1996), and served as director at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (attested 1996).
Hoong Teik Toh specializes in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Toh earned a PhD from Harvard University in 2004, having studied under teachers Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu.

Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales (1900–1981) worked in archaeology and Indology. He earned a bachelor's at Queens' College, Cambridge, and a PhD at SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden; he held posts at King's College Bangkok, Greater India Society, and Royal Asiatic Society.

Horace Hayman Wilson (1786–1860) was an Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital. He held posts at the East India Company, the Calcutta Mint, and was Boden Professor of Sanscrit at the University of Oxford from 1831 to 1860.

Horace L. Friess (1900–1975) worked in religious studies and philosophy. He earned his bachelor's from Columbia University, also studying at Heidelberg University, and held posts at Johns Hopkins and Columbia, where he was appointed a professor from 1962 to 1966.
Horkhang Sonam Palbar (1919–1995) was a scholar in Tibetology. He studied under Tsadru Ngawang Losang and was a student of Gendun Chophel from circa 1946 to 1951.
Horst Brinkhaus is an Indologist who held academic posts at the University of Münster (circa 1974–1980) and Kiel University (circa 1993–2011).

Horst Lasic is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Vienna in 1999. Lasic served as a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1995) and taught at Vienna (1999).

Hosakote Krishna Sastri (1870–1928) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held appointments at the Archaeological Survey of India (circa 1891–1925) and served as Government Epigraphist for India from circa 1920 to 1925.

Hoseok Leigh is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Leigh completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010), having studied under teacher Ha-u Kim and traditional teacher Cheonghwa.
Hoseong Kim (born 1960) works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Kim founded the Nihon Bukkyōshi Kenkyūjo and has served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2011).
Hoshu Mitsuhara (1928–2008) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor (attested 1982) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2004) at Koyasan University.

Hotetsu Matsumoto (b. 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Matsumoto held a post at Tohoku University (attested 1997) and became a professor and center director at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).
